Definition: from G4134; to make replete, i.e. (literally) to cram (a net), level up (a hollow), or (figuratively) to furnish (or imbue, diffuse, influence), satisfy, execute (an office), finish (a period or task), verify (or coincide with a prediction), etc.:--accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, make) full (come), fully preach, perfect, supply.
BiblicalUsage: Pleroo means to fill, to fulfil, to make full. Jesus came not to destroy the law but to fulfil it, in Matthew 5:17, and Matthew 1:22 says all this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet. His joy is fulfilled in us in John 15:11, and we are to be filled with the Spirit in Ephesians 5:18. All the law is fulfilled in one word, says Galatians 5:14: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus fills everything He touches — prophecy, law, joy, and the empty heart. My position is that He did not come to leave things half-done, and He will not leave me half-filled.
